subject: Partner contract variance / triage: BrightCrest MSA + SOW
messages:
From: Ellen Morris <emorris@brightcrest.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@brightcrest.com>, Tom Gallagher <tg@brightcrest.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightCrest - MSA + SOW redlines (first pass)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attaching our redlined MSA and a lightly annotated SOW for the initial integration engagement. Key asks summarized below so your team can triage:

- Data processing: we requested a DPA section in the MSA (see §4) that limits data use to the purposes of providing the service and prohibits model training on customer data.
- Audit rights: we propose quarterly audit access for SOC evidence and limited on-site review language.
- Indemnity: we added a carveout for third-party IP claims originating from partner tooling.
- SLA / credits: we pushed for a 99.9% uptime SLA with token-based credits for breaches.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the DPA wording and whether there’s any objection to the audit cadence? If not, please flag the specific clauses (MSA pages 2–6) you want to escalate and we’ll try to be flexible on indemnity and SLA in exchange for narrower audit scope.

Attachments: BrightCrest_MSA_Redline_v3.pdf, BrightCrest_SOW_v1_marked.docx

Best,
Ellen Morris

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCrest - MSA + SOW redlines (first pass)

Ellen —

Thanks for sending these so quickly and for the clear summary. I’m looping in Monica (legal) and Ben (partner ops/procurement) to triage the items below. High-level responses:

1) DPA / model training prohibition: Redwood’s standard position for hosted customers is to provide an explicit DPA clause that restricts training on customer data. We should be able to accept language that ties data use to "providing the service" and explicitly forbids usage for training/updating models without written consent. Monica, can you confirm the exact phrasing we should propose back?

2) Audit rights: quarterly audits are heavier than our typical approach. We can offer annual audits with an option for ad-hoc audits upon reasonable cause and mutual NDA. Monica, if you think a quarterly cadence is necessary, please flag the minimal scope we could agree to (logs only? redacted samples?).

3) Indemnity/IP: can probably accept tighter carveouts for partner tooling if BrightCrest accepts a mutual indemnity cap tied to the contract value. Ben — this will affect procurement risk scoring; can you run potential commercial hold implications?

Next steps: Monica to propose redline language for DPA/audit/indemnity. Ben to confirm procurement impact and whether we need to involve Finance for a special exception. I’ll monitor with BrightCrest and keep the timeline tight — they indicated they want to finalize ahead of their board meeting next week.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
+1 415 555 2104

Attachments referenced: BrightCrest_MSA_Redline_v3.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Morris <emorris@brightcrest.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: RE: BrightCrest - MSA + SOW redlines (first pass)

Folks —

I reviewed the BrightCrest redlines and sketched a balanced counterproposal. Summary of recommended positions (high priority first):

- DPA / model-training clause: Acceptable if we insert an explicit exception for system telemetry and aggregated non-identifiable usage metrics. Proposed language: "Customer Data will not be used to train or improve Redwood models, except for aggregated, de-identified telemetry necessary for service operation and safety, as described in Exhibit A." This preserves operations while addressing their training concern.

- Audit rights: Offer annual audit with up to two days remote evidence review per year. For additional audits, require reasonable cause and cost-sharing. If they insist on on-site access, limit to log review and provide redacted samples — no direct access to our internal model weights or training environments.

- Indemnity & cap: Propose reciprocal indemnity with cap equal to 12 months of recurring fees (standard customer carve). Carveouts for willful misconduct remain. For partner tooling IP claims, propose a triage step: partner provides indemnity if claim arises from partner-supplied integrations.

- SLA: We can accept a 99.9% target but request a sliding credit schedule and exclusion for scheduled maintenance and force majeure.

I attached a marked-up counterproposal (Redwood_Counterproposal_v1.docx). Happy to walk through live. If BrightCrest needs more aggressive audit cadence, we should connect Security for a technical attestation rather than ongoing quarterly audits.

Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_Counterproposal_v1.docx

Team —

Quick procurement read: the proposed indemnity cap and audit asks will likely require an approval from Sales Ops and Finance for anything above our 'standard' threshold (we treat 6 months recurring as typical; Monica's 12 months cap is outside standard but not unprecedented). Three items for sales to confirm:

1) Estimated ARR from initial 12-month SOW: $420k (forecast).
2) Any onboarding professional services that are one-time (impacts cap calculation).
3) Whether BrightCrest expects a discount tied to the tighter SLA / audit windows (they asked for aggressive SLA; if we accept, ask for a 7–10% price uplift or a one-time security attestation fee).

If Sales Ops signs off, Finance will clear the 12-month cap. If not, we need to push for 6 months cap + security attestation. I can coordinate a quick call with BrightCrest procurement tomorrow to align expectations. Vivek, want me to set that up?

Ben Carter
Director, Partner Operations (Americas)
ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: 2027-06-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCrest - MSA + SOW redlines (first pass)

Vivek / Monica / Ben —

Thanks for the rapid review and concrete counterproposal. BrightCrest is comfortable with the following compromise:

- DPA: Accept Redwood's proposed exception for aggregated, de-identified telemetry.
- Audit: Accept annual remote evidence review + ad-hoc audits for cause with cost-sharing.
- Indemnity cap: BrightCrest will accept a mutual cap of 12 months recurring fees if Redwood agrees to a one-time security attestation (we don’t require quarterly audits if we get the attestation).
- SLA: Agree to the sliding credit schedule and exclusions for scheduled maintenance.

We attach a short acceptance memo and the attestation we’d like Redwood to provide (BrightCrest_Acceptance_Attestation.pdf). Please confirm whether Redwood can generate the attestation document by end of day Friday so we can route to our internal approvals committee. If it helps, we can proceed with DocuSign once we have the final MSA + SOW redlines.

Thanks — this feels like good progress. Vivek — please confirm next steps and timeline.

Best,
Ellen Morris
Sr. Counsel, BrightCrest Analytics

Attachments: BrightCrest_Acceptance_Attestation.pdf
